requirements.requirement: On node1, /tmp must ignore program execution, setuid bits, and device nodes, with the settings surviving reboot.
requirements.summary: Before reboot, /tmp was a tmpfs mounted with nosuid,nodev,noexec. After a confirmed reboot with a changed boot ID, those options remained active; direct execution returned 126, device-node access failed, mode remained 1777, and the persistent fstab entry validated successfully.

requirements.requirement: On node1, /dev/shm must ignore program execution, setuid bits, and device nodes, with the settings surviving reboot.
requirements.summary: Before reboot, /dev/shm was a tmpfs mounted with nosuid,nodev,noexec. After the confirmed reboot, those options remained active; direct execution returned 126, device-node access failed, mode remained 1777, and the persistent fstab entry validated successfully.

overall_summary: Both requested mounts are hardened with nosuid,nodev,noexec and were directly verified after a real node restart. The restart protocol is complete: node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged the scheduled reboot, changed boot identity from 4d340bf4-0579-47f0-98c1-5c17a66d50f1 to d24a7942-bec5-4a7c-b418-bb246953fc92, returned to system state running with zero failed units, and retained the hardened mounts.
limitations: The nosuid behavior was established by the directly observed mount option, but no isolated setuid execution test was possible because noexec independently prevents execution on both mounts.
The lifecycle inventory does not inspect /etc directly, so continued presence of the safety backup /etc/fstab.pre-mount-hardening is inferred from its creation and absence of a removal command.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The fstab backup and edits were bounded safety/configuration actions; daemon reload, mounting, and the corrective /dev/shm remount directly established the required state. Test scripts and device nodes were removed after each bounded check. The required reboot completed cleanly, with no failed services, unchanged listening-service exposure, and healthy package state. Temporary-file changes are expected consequences of mounting /tmp as tmpfs and rebooting.
